Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman with 3-day history of red, dry, intensely pruritic rash on hands and forearms after swimming; clinical impression of contact/irritant dermatitis, plan for topical steroid, emollient, and OTC antihistamine with 1-week review.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dry, itchy skin on arms and hands.
- Onset/Timeline: Began a few days ago; noticed soon after a recent swim; progressive pruritus, unchanged/red despite coconut-butter use.
- Associated symptoms: No spots/pustules, no cracking, no discharge/bleeding, no fevers, sweats, vomiting, diarrhea, or urinary issues. Reports feeling tired; appetite and hydration normal.
- Pertinent negatives: No facial, chest, or leg involvement; no systemic illness.
- PMH: Denies prior eczema/dermatitis or other chronic disease. Possible lactose intolerance.
- Medications: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive); no other regular meds.
- Allergies: None to medications; self-reported lactose intolerance.
- Family history: Father asthma; mother hay fever; no known familial skin disorders.
- Social / preventive: Lives alone; primary-school teacher; high work stress; non-smoker; minimal alcohol; no recreational drugs; recent swimming exposure.

Examination:
- Remote consultation—no in-person exam performed.
- Patient-reported findings: Erythematous, dry, pruritic rash limited to dorsal hands and forearms.
- No systemic signs; vitals not obtained.

Impression:
- Most likely: Irritant contact dermatitis secondary to chlorine exposure (acute onset post-swim, localized to exposed skin, red/pruritic, no prior history).
- Alternate considerations:
  • Atopic dermatitis flare (family atopy, stress/dry weather) – less likely given first episode and clear exposure trigger.
  • Allergic contact dermatitis to pool chemicals/other products – possible but presentation favors irritant mechanism.

Plan:
- Provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis.
- Topical therapy: Prescribe low- to moderate-potency corticosteroid cream for affected areas twice daily for 7 days.
- Skin care: Frequent application of bland emollient throughout day.
- Symptomatic relief: Recommend OTC oral antihistamine (e.g., cetirizine or loratadine) for itch.
- Advice: Avoid further swimming/chlorine exposure and use gentle, fragrance-free soaps; monitor for spreading, weeping, or infection.
- Follow-up: Re-assessment in 1 week if no improvement or sooner if worsening.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing elements: Specific steroid name/strength, dosing instructions documented; drug allergy list confirmation; objective skin exam and vitals; formal follow-up appointment date.
● Conflicts: None significant—DDx emphasizes irritant contact dermatitis; transcript labels “dermatitis” without specifying type (no direct conflict).
● Transcript quality: Generally clear, minor inaudible words; no physical examination performed, limiting objective data.
